What do the five levels mean?

A square is magic when its rows, columns and both principal diagonals share one sum. Bimagic also requires equal sums of squares; trimagic adds cubes; tetramagic adds fourth powers; pentamagic adds fifth powers.

Each level includes all preceding levels. Equal fifth-power sums alone do not establish pentamagicity.

Normality and large files

Normality means each integer from 1 through N² occurs exactly once. Consecutive entries can start at any integer, including 0 or a negative value. Sequential here describes the entry set, not the order of entries in each row. The report also shows repetitions and missing integers between the minimum and maximum.

Files are read in chunks, and calculations run in a background worker. The checker retains column sums rather than the whole matrix. Very large files can take considerable time; Cancel stops the calculation. Normality is checked for up to 500 million entries. Shifted and non-normal inputs receive an additional entry-set pass. Extremely sparse ranges with over one million distinct values are clearly marked as only partially checked.

Verification result

Downloads include exact sums, classifications, entry-set checks, optional block counts and up to 20 unequal-line examples per power. For large sums, use TXT or JSON to preserve precision; spreadsheet programs may round CSV numbers when opening them.

Exact power sums

The reference is the first row’s sum. Every other required line must match it. The normal target applies to entries 1–N².

Scope: rows, columns and both principal diagonals. Optional blocks are aligned and non-overlapping. Sliding blocks and broken diagonals are not tested.

Credits and mathematical sources

Checker and presentation: Inder J. Taneja. Example seeds: Georges Pfeffermann (order 8), Walter Trump (order 12), and Toshihiro Shirakawa (orders 64 and 512). The Shirakawa examples are normalized to start at 1 when needed.
